items.title: One Day Trip to Tiruvannamalai Part 2 | Arunachala Temple & Food Vlog | MonkVlogs
items.description:
#foodtour #tiruvannamalai #annamalaiyar 

Welcome to Part 2 of Monkvlogs’ brand-new One Day Trip series! 🚗🙏

In this concept, Foodymonk picks a destination within 150–200 km from Bengaluru and explores it completely in a single day — covering places to visit, temples, interesting spots, hidden food gems, local eateries and everything worth experiencing along the way.

In Part 1, we started our journey from Bengaluru at 5 AM, visited the historic Chandra Choodeshwarar Temple in Hosur, enjoyed bre
items.why_watch: FoodyMonk's one-day trip format is genuinely useful — he caps destinations at 150–200 km from Bengaluru, making the itinerary actually replicable on a weekend. This episode focuses on Arunachala Temple in Tiruvannamalai and weaves in hyper-local food stops that most travel guides skip entirely. If you're planning a South India road trip or just want to experience a major pilgrimage town without the overwhelm, this is a practical ground-level preview.

discovery_articles.title: The Rabbit Hole, Rue Jankowski in Le Mans, France
discovery_articles.snippet: Rue Jankowski is a dead end in Le Mans' Saint-Nicolas district, the kind of narrow passage you'd normally walk past without a second look. Then you turn the corner and the wall seems to fall away into a glowing, striped tunnel, arcing across the buildings around it as though the street itself had been punched open. The piece is called Rabbit Hole, painted in May and June 2022 by the Parisian street artist Seth as guest of honor at Le Mans' urban art festival, Plein Champ.

discovery_articles.title: Parque Ciudad de las Canteras (Quarry City Park) in Oaxaca, Mexico
discovery_articles.snippet: The nickname "Green Antequera" for the Mexican city of Oaxaca de Juárez might seem strange at first: is it related to the vegetation of the valley it sits in and the mountains that surround it during the wet season? Walking in its historical center, though, the "green" part becomes clearer as this is the color of the rock that forms many of the buildings here, and even the sidewalks. This rock is known as "cantera", which is also the Spanish word for "quarry".

discovery_articles.title: Giant Puppet Parade in Siem Reap, Cambodia
discovery_articles.snippet: Being a child in Cambodia is likely to be rough. By many counts, the country is one of the poorest in Asia, leading to high rates of child abandonment and even orphaning. It is also one of the most heavily-landmined countries, a legacy of 20th-century conflicts like the Vietnam War and the Khmer Rouge regime, which means that many children will often have had an amputation or explosion-related incident.

Perhaps surprisingly, though, most of them are frozen: our daughters eat them straight from the freezer most evenings, with frozen berries and yoghurt, for pudding. We normally order a stack of bananas every Saturday, and before the end of the week they inevitably start to turn brown.
